general_information.Description: This course is designed to supplement Interpretation 1 through offering more advanced theoretical approaches to interpretation, ensuring an advanced understanding of professional interpreting practice. By providing a guidance in developing sufficient background knowledge in subject areas for interpreting, students are expected to be equipped with experience of dealing with problems in interpreting at the advanced level, being capable of working in various interpreting settings.
general_information.StudentTasks: - Attend at least 80% of contact hours in order to be accepted to the final examination - Actively participate in class activities - Fulfill tasks given by the teacher after class - Use their own laptops in class only for learning purposes - Read the textbook in advance
general_information.Tools: 1. Ted-Ed: (choose clips with no Vietsub provided) 2. Viet Nam News: (choose articles related to politics, science, nature, lifestyle, healthcare) 3. CNN: (choose clips and articles related to science, nature, lifestyle, healthcare) 4. ABC: (choose clips and articles related to science, nature, lifestyle, healthcare)

description: This course is designed to supplement Interpretation 1 through offering more advanced theoretical approaches to interpretation, ensuring an advanced understanding of professional interpreting practice. By providing a guidance in developing sufficient background knowledge in subject areas for interpreting, students are expected to be equipped with experience of dealing with problems in interpreting at the advanced level, being capable of working in various interpreting settings.

learning_outcomes.CLO Details: Identify the issue that some meanings could not be brought out totally and how to improvise by using equivalents.
Understand the role of logic and emotion when argueing and the professionalism of interpreters when interpreting arguments.
Understand the importance of word choice and how to handle shades of language.
Understand the strategies to interprete in formal situations with a proper consideration to balance the language richness.
Identify the challenges posed by the interpretation of policy address.
Have a well-developed political and/or economic knowledge in order to successfully convey the meaning of related problems.
Identitfy challenges when conveying the concept of humour.
Understand how to deal with tasks that involve the use of Latin.
Understand the value of teamwork skills and attitudes in interpretation.
Deeply and broadly understand the principles of advanced interpretation, and master interpreting skills used for various fields and settings.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in all 9 units of the course to interpreting in a business setting.
assessments.Note: Teacher is asked to write a field trip proposal with specific details and send it to the person in charge; or organize a project that facilitates the subject.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in the delivered units (Units 1-3) to consecutive interpreting.
assessments.Note: The teacher will prepare a text for each student (≈100words/text), and inform students the topics of those texts in advance. The student shall prepare materials related to the topics to facilitate interpreting performance. On the test day, each pair of students will randomly pick 2 texts and take turns to read and interpret.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in the delivered units (Units 4-6) to consecutive interpreting.
assessments.Note: The teacher will prepare a text for each student (≈100words/text), and inform students the topics of those texts in advance. The student shall prepare materials related to the topics to facilitate interpreting performance. On the test day, each pair of students will randomly pick 2 texts and take turns to read and interpret.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test the student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in the delivered units (Units 7-9) to simultaneous interpreting.
assessments.Note: The teacher shall prepare 5-6 audio files (≈2minutes/file) relating to several specific topics, of which the students will be informed in advance. On the test day, students will be divided into groups of 4 or 5. All members will be standing at different positions in class, simultaneously listening to the same audio and recording their interpretation using a smartphone. Upon completion, students are asked to send the record to the teacher immediately.

assessments.Knowledge and Skill: Test student's ability to apply knowledge and techniques obtained in all 9 units of the course to consecutive interpreting (both ENG-VIE and VIE-ENG processes). Topics: 1. Education 2. Entertainment 3. Technology 4. Environment/Nature 5. Business, Economics and Finance 6. Tourism 7. Family and Friends 8. Health 9. Culture 10. Arts
assessments.Note: The length of one audio is 220-250 words. Students take the exam individually. Students will randomly pick 2 topics to interpret. Students will listen to one audio in English for E-V interpretation, and listen to audio or the examiners reading a text in Vietnamese for the V-E process. Students are allowed to take notes in the exam room.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ1
constructive_questions.Details: What do you consider Untranslatability in interpretation? What factors leading to this?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ2
constructive_questions.Details: What are some possible solutions to deal with the untranslatability? How do you use equivalents in dealing with the untranslatability?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ3
constructive_questions.Details: What will be considered the Untranslatability in your speech about customs and habit of English-speaking countries? Deliver your full speech (in Eng) about some customs and habits of one English-speaking country you like. Your speech will be interpret by other groups.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ4
constructive_questions.Details: Anticipate some untranslatability in the interpretation of talk shows regarding the similarities and differences between Vietnamese culture and American culture (in some specific aspects). As presenters, present your research findings in the form of a talk show (Eng or Vie). As interpreters, interpret the talk show into Vie or Eng.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ5
constructive_questions.Details: Based on a translated document about cultural value preservation (Vie-Eng), what are some untranslatable contents in the source text? How are these dealt with in the translated document? Do you agree or disagree with the solutions?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ6
constructive_questions.Details: What are some untranslatable contents in a movie? Analyze how a movie clip (10 minute clip) has been interpreted? How does the interpreter deal with the untranslatability? Choose another 10 minute clip to interpret.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ7
constructive_questions.Details: What factors make an argument? Consider an argument made by a politician and identify how are the logic and emotion expressed in the argument?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ8
constructive_questions.Details: How should professionalism be achieved in the interpretation of an argument?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ9
constructive_questions.Details: Imagine you are delivering a speech in order to advocate a change in a law which you consider foolish. What arguments would you use? In what order? From the simplest to the most complex, or vice-versa? What evidence could you offer in support of your proposal? How would you refute any counter-arguments you might anticipate? As speakers, deliver your speech. Your speech will be interpreted by interpreters.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ10
constructive_questions.Details: Based on an argument on immigration (in English) made by a politician, analyze how the argument has been made? What problems you may face in the interpretation of this? How will the argument be interpreted?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ11
constructive_questions.Details: In the interpretation of an argument, it is critical for an interpreter to carefully follow every step in the speaker's train of thought. Do you agree or disagree? Take an argument on poverty topic made by a politician and interpret it.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ12
constructive_questions.Details: What are some lessons in the interpretation of arguments? Consider an argument on housing problem made by a Vietnamese politician, how should it be interpreted into English?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ13
constructive_questions.Details: How should diction and register be dealt with in interpretation?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ14
constructive_questions.Details: What problems do diction and register may generate for interpreters?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ15
constructive_questions.Details: Based on a given text about Tourism, analyze the register used, and identify how you interpret it.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ16
constructive_questions.Details: Are different types of register interpreted differently? Analyze 3 audios or clips about negotiation in business, expressed in different types (at least 3) of register and choose suitable ways of interpretation for each.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ17
constructive_questions.Details: Based on a translated document about protectionist measures (Eng-Vie), identify what types of register are used in the original text? How has the text been interpreted?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ18
constructive_questions.Details: You are going to make a speech to persuade audience to buy your business's products. What types of register are you using? How are they used? Your speech will be interpreted into Vie or Eng.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ19
constructive_questions.Details: Review the interpretation of Untranslatability, Argumentation, and Diction/Register. What impacts do these have on interpretation. Make a presentation (in Vietnamese) one of the topics related to business, tourism... in which there are features of untranslatability, argumentation, diction/register. Your presentation will be interpreted.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ20
constructive_questions.Details: What are differences in dealing with Untranslatability, Argumentation, and Diction/Register. Make an argument for or against a controversial issue related to business or tourism which includes some features of untranslatability, some types of register.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ21
constructive_questions.Details: What are some differences between formal and informal styles?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ22
constructive_questions.Details: What are some factors generating formal style?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ23
constructive_questions.Details: What are some requirements for the interpretation of formal style speech?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ24
constructive_questions.Details: Based on a given English speech, identify factors generating the formality of the speech? How are these interpreted?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ25
constructive_questions.Details: Based on a given Vietnamese speech, identify factors generating the formality of the speech? How are these interpreted?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ26
constructive_questions.Details: Analyze a speech given by a politician. What makes it a formal oratory? How should it be interpreted?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ27
constructive_questions.Details: What possible problems may policy address cause to interpreters?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ28
constructive_questions.Details: How are challenges caused by policy address dealt with in interpretation?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ29
constructive_questions.Details: Study a given speech made by a politician about international relations. How are the words and structures highlighted in bold type going to be treated? Find the equivalents for these words and structures.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ30
constructive_questions.Details: You are given a speech made by a Vietnamese Public Health Ministry. Consider specific challenges related to words, phrases, structures you may face in the interpretation. How are you going to treat these? interpret the speech into English.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ31
constructive_questions.Details: Consecutive Interpreting Practice: Health Care Imagine you are delivering a speech (In Eng.) to persuade parents to get their children vaccinated. What tone will your speech carry? What words, phrases, structures may cause problems for interpreters? Your speech is interpreted by other groups.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ32
constructive_questions.Details: What words, phrases, structures are common in speeches related to diplomacy and health care? What are their equivalents in Vietnamese? Organize a meeting discussing solutions to prevent the infection of viruses. Your meeting will be interpreted into Vietnamese or English.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ33
constructive_questions.Details: What challenges does a political discourse posed to interpreters? Analyze a discourse to clarify those problems.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ34
constructive_questions.Details: What are some requirements for the interpretation of a political discourse? It is argued that "translators act as mediators in situations of political conflicts". Do you agree or disagree?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ35
constructive_questions.Details: Based on a given political discourse (English version). Topic: International conflict. Identify possible problems interpreters face in the interpretation of the discourse. How do you interpret discourse?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ36
constructive_questions.Details: What are common terms frequently used in English political discourses related to labor force? How are they translated into Vietnamese? Make a political discourse using those terms. Your speech is interpreted by other groups.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ37
constructive_questions.Details: What are similarities and differences between a Vietnamese political discourse and an English political discourse? Do they cause similar or different problems in interpretation? Analyze a Vietnamese political discourse, topic: solutions to unemployment, and interpret it into English.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ38
constructive_questions.Details: What are main parts of a political speech? What purpose does each part perform? How should each part be dealt with in interpretation? Analyze and interpret a political discourse (English version). Topic: Solutions to unemployment.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ39
constructive_questions.Details: Review political discourse: Which part of a political discourse is more difficult to be interpreted? What are the reasons for this? How is the given political discourse interpreted? (Eng-Vie, Topic:politics)

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ40
constructive_questions.Details: Review political discourse: What are common words, phrase, structures used in political speeches? Which translation method is used more frequently in the interpretation of this? Make a political speech in Vietnamese with full of 5 parts for the other group to interpret into English. Topic: Politics

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ41
constructive_questions.Details: "Writings and oral presentations on economics can be highly technical", what features of an economic discourse make it difficult for interpretation?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ42
constructive_questions.Details: How important is it to master economics-related terms and jargons in interpretation?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ43
constructive_questions.Details: You are going to interpret an audio/clip on " Tariffs". What terms and jargons are needed to study in advance? Interpret the clip/audio into Vietnamese.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ44
constructive_questions.Details: You are going to interpret an audio/clip on " Business Risks". What terms and jargons are needed to study in advance? Interpret the clip/audio into English.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ45
constructive_questions.Details: Why is it difficult to convey sense of humor in interpretation?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ46
constructive_questions.Details: What problems interpreters may face in the interpretation of humor?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ47
constructive_questions.Details: Are there some universal humors all over the world? Analyze such a story and demonstrate how you interpret it.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ48
constructive_questions.Details: What are common topics for humorous stories? What are typical words, phrases, and structurers for the interpretation of these? What are their equivalents? Illustrate these by interpreting a humorous story.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ49
constructive_questions.Details: What types of texts often use Latin expressions? What are the differences among 3 types of Latinism?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ50
constructive_questions.Details: What problems does Latin expressions cause for interpreters? How is each type of Latinism coped with in interpretation?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ51
constructive_questions.Details: What Latin expressions are common in technical texts? What are their equivalents in Vietnamese? Analyze a technical speech and demonstrate how you interpret it into Vietnamese?

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ52
constructive_questions.Details: How are prefixes and suffixes important in identifying the meaning of technical terms? What are typical prefixes and suffixes in technical English? What are their equivalents? Analyze a technical speech and interpret it into Vietnamese.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ53
constructive_questions.Details: Review: What different approaches are used to deal with the interpretation of different source texts including humorous stories, technical issues, economic discourses. Make a speech in Vietnamese. Topic: humor stories, technical issues, or economic discourse. Your speech will be interpreted into English.

constructive_questions.Name: HN_CQ54
constructive_questions.Details: Review: What are you going to do with technical terms whose equivalents can't be found in Vietnamese? What are typical technical terms whose equivalents can't be found in Vietnamese? Make a speech in English. Topic: Technical issue. Your speech will be interpreted into Vietnamese.
